subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does the reporter have a private reproduction showing an unauthenticated or differently authenticated peer injecting frames into an established Gateway WebSocket connection despite the connect challenge, device authorization, and authenticated dispatcher?
rationale: Source inspection contradicts the proposed sequence-ID attack, but protected security handling should not dismiss a potentially omitted transport or authentication prerequisite without explicit owner confirmation.

options.title: Request private exploit proof
options.body: Ask for a minimal private reproduction identifying attacker position, authentication state, captured frame, and the authorization boundary crossed before deciding whether remediation is needed.

options.title: Close as unsupported
options.body: Close after a gateway security owner confirms that sequence values are only per-socket ordering metadata and no omitted injection prerequisite exists.

recommendation.title: Request private exploit proof
recommendation.body: Ask for a minimal private reproduction identifying attacker position, authentication state, captured frame, and the authorization boundary crossed before deciding whether remediation is needed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate connected to Gateway-backed client protocol semantics and can coordinate the appropriate security owner if needed.
